newsitem.title: UK: Future US air cargo trade index up 4.4pct in Aug.
newsitem.headline: Future US air cargo trade index up 4.4pct in Aug.

text.p: The index of future U.S. air cargo business rose 4.4 percent to 504.8 in August, compared to a 1.4 percent gain in July, the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi said.

In its latest Foreign Trade survey of air freight carriers, seaports and trucking firms released here on Wednesday, the bank's New York economic research department said this was the largest increase for air cargo since the 4.5 percent rise seen in September 1995.
The overall index of future business for all transport modes showed a 2.1 percent gain in August to 403.5, the biggest rise since March last year when it jumped 3.2 percent.

The three month forward looking index said air cargo export expectations were up 3.8 percent in the month to 620, against a 0.4 percent rise in July, and the sharpest rise since the 5.7 percent recorded in February 1995.
There was also a steep jump in air cargo import expectations which gained 5.5 percent, up from 3.1 percent the previous month. The previous higher gain was six percent in September 1995.
However the August index of current air cargo trade acitivity was unchanged at 413.1 percent, unchanged on the previous month.
The index is an equally weighted composite index of current export and import activity air cargo activity (not seasonally adjusted and 1989 equals 100).
In August both current export and import conditions were unchanged against respective falls of 1.4 percent and 1.9 percent, the survey said.

Commenting on the survey, it said that one Asian-based air cargo company noted U.S. exports of large infrastructure items bound for Asia are expected to slow as they were hearing of fewer orders being placed. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017
